ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows the variation curve of the one-dimensional electric field E between A and B with position x. Near A and near B, the electric field is 0; the middle nonzero part linearly increases from 20 kV/cm on the left side to 40 kV/cm on the right side, and the horizontal width of the nonzero interval is labeled as 5 μm. Reasoning: The potential difference satisfies ψ_B - ψ_A = -∫_A^B E dx. According to the specified method, regard the nonzero region as a trapezoid, with parallel sides 20 kV/cm and 40 kV/cm, and width 5 μm = 5×10^-4 cm. Area = [(20+40)/2] kV/cm × 5×10^-4 cm = 30×5×10^-4 kV = 0.015 kV = 15 V. Since the potential decreases along the positive electric field direction, ψ_B - ψ_A = -15 V.

method.method_draft: Treat the shaded/nonzero part of the E-x graph as a trapezoid with parallel sides 20 and 40 kV/cm and width 5 μm. Compute area = [(20+40)/2] kV/cm × 5×10^-4 cm = 0.015 kV = 15 V. Since potential decreases in the direction of positive electric field, ψ_B - ψ_A = -15 V.

method.method_draft: Split the field area into a rectangle of height 20 kV/cm and width 5 μm plus a triangle of height 20 kV/cm and base 5 μm. Convert width: 5 μm = 5×10^-4 cm. Rectangle area = 20×5×10^-4 kV = 0.010 kV = 10 V. Triangle area = 1/2×20×5×10^-4 kV = 0.005 kV = 5 V. Total ∫E dx = 15 V, so ψ_B - ψ_A = -15 V.
